## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Quaternion arithmetic and construction
//
// Portable reference bodies for the quaternion operations that used to be host
// intrinsics. Every formula is a faithful port of System.Numerics.Quaternion
// (https://github.com/microsoft/referencesource — System.Numerics/Quaternion.cs),
// including operand order and branch structure, so host and portable evaluation
// agree bit-for-bit.
//
// The rotation *conversions* (axis-angle, Euler, rotor, matrix embeddings) live in
// `transforms.library.plato`; this file holds only the algebra and the
// three `Create*` constructors.
//
// https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternions_and_spatial_rotation

library RotationsOps
{
    //==
    // Magnitude and normalization

    // The dot product of the two quaternions, taken over all four components.
    Dot(self: Quaternion, quaternion2: Quaternion): Number
        => self.X * quaternion2.X + self.Y * quaternion2.Y
         + self.Z * quaternion2.Z + self.W * quaternion2.W;

    // The squared magnitude: the dot product with itself. Cheaper than Length,
    // and the form comparisons should prefer.
    LengthSquared(self: Quaternion): Number
        => self.Dot(self);

    // The magnitude of the quaternion. A rotation quaternion has length 1.
    Length(self: Quaternion): Number
        => self.LengthSquared.Sqrt;

    // Rescale to unit magnitude, restoring the rotation invariant after repeated
    // products. Precondition: the quaternion is not zero.
    Normalize(self: Quaternion): Quaternion
        => self * (1.0 / self.Length);

    //==
    // Conjugation and inversion

    // The conjugate: the vector part negated. For a unit quaternion this is the
    // inverse (the opposite rotation).
    Conjugate(self: Quaternion): Quaternion
        => (-self.X, -self.Y, -self.Z, self.W);

    // The multiplicative inverse: the conjugate divided by the squared magnitude.
    // Precondition: the quaternion is not zero.
    Inverse(self: Quaternion): Quaternion {
        var invNorm = 1.0 / self.LengthSquared;
        return (-self.X * invNorm, -self.Y * invNorm, -self.Z * invNorm, self.W * invNorm);
    }

    //==
    // Component-wise algebra

    // Component-wise sum. Not a rotation composition; the result is generally not
    // a unit quaternion.
    Add(a: Quaternion, b: Quaternion): Quaternion
        => (a.X + b.X, a.Y + b.Y, a.Z + b.Z, a.W + b.W);

    // Component-wise difference.
    Subtract(a: Quaternion, b: Quaternion): Quaternion
        => (a.X - b.X, a.Y - b.Y, a.Z - b.Z, a.W - b.W);

    // All four components negated. Encodes the same rotation as the original
    // (q and -q are the double cover of the same orientation).
    Negative(a: Quaternion): Quaternion
        => (-a.X, -a.Y, -a.Z, -a.W);

    // Uniform scaling of all four components.
    Multiply(a: Quaternion, scalar: Number): Quaternion
        => (a.X * scalar, a.Y * scalar, a.Z * scalar, a.W * scalar);

    //==
    // Rotation composition

    // The Hamilton product, in System.Numerics operand order: the vector parts
    // give a cross term plus the scalar-weighted vectors, and the scalar part
    // loses the vector dot product.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternion#Hamilton_product
    Multiply(a: Quaternion, b: Quaternion): Quaternion {
        var cx = a.Y * b.Z - a.Z * b.Y;
        var cy = a.Z * b.X - a.X * b.Z;
        var cz = a.X * b.Y - a.Y * b.X;
        var dot = a.X * b.X + a.Y * b.Y + a.Z * b.Z;
        return (a.X * b.W + b.X * a.W + cx,
                a.Y * b.W + b.Y * a.W + cy,
                a.Z * b.W + b.Z * a.W + cz,
                a.W * b.W - dot);
    }

    // Multiplication by the inverse of `b` — component-for-component the
    // referencesource body, which inlines Inverse into the Hamilton product.
    // Precondition: `b` is not zero.
    Divide(a: Quaternion, b: Quaternion): Quaternion
        => a * b.Inverse;

    // The rotation that applies `self` first and then `value2`. Note the reversed
    // operand order against Multiply: Concatenate(v1, v2) = v2 * v1.
    Concatenate(self: Quaternion, value2: Quaternion): Quaternion
        => value2 * self;

    //==
    // Interpolation

    // Normalized linear interpolation along the shorter arc: the operands are
    // taken with opposite signs when their dot product is negative, and the
    // component-wise blend is renormalized. `amount` is unclamped.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slerp#Quaternion_slerp
    Lerp(self: Quaternion, quaternion2: Quaternion, amount: Number): Quaternion {
        var t1 = 1.0 - amount;
        var blend = self.Dot(quaternion2) >= 0.0
            ? self * t1 + quaternion2 * amount
            : self * t1 - quaternion2 * amount;
        return blend.Normalize;
    }

    // Spherical linear interpolation along the shorter arc: constant angular
    // velocity, falling back to the plain (unnormalized) linear blend when the
    // operands are within 1e-6 of parallel and the sine of the angle is unusable.
    // `amount` is unclamped.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slerp
    Slerp(self: Quaternion, quaternion2: Quaternion, amount: Number): Quaternion {
        var d = self.Dot(quaternion2);
        var flip = d < 0.0;
        // The magnitude, not `flip ? -d : d`: the two spellings agree, but the
        // conditional's branches erase differently under `--scalar=float` and the
        // C# writer cannot type the result (CS0172).
        var cosOmega = d.Abs;
        var omega = cosOmega.AcosRadians;
        var invSinOmega = 1.0 / omega.Sin;
        var nearlyParallel = cosOmega > 0.999999;
        var s1 = nearlyParallel
            ? 1.0 - amount
            : ((1.0 - amount) * omega).Sin * invSinOmega;
        var s2 = nearlyParallel
            ? amount
            : (amount * omega).Sin * invSinOmega;
        return self * s1 + quaternion2 * (flip ? -s2 : s2);
    }

    //==
    // Hashing

    // The component hashes folded together.
    Hash(self: Quaternion): Integer
        => self.X.Hash
            .CombineHash(self.Y.Hash)
            .CombineHash(self.Z.Hash)
            .CombineHash(self.W.Hash);
```
